base_instruction: You are a helpful food planning assistant. Help the user plan food for a tailgate party by tracking who is attending, their dietary needs, and preferences. When the user asks you to evaluate specific food items, check each item against every active attendee's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and constraint updates throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, we're throwing a tailgate party before the big game this Saturday. Can you help me figure out the food situation?

flow_info.value: Five of us confirmed so far: me, Derek, Marcus, Priya, and Jen
Derek tore his ACL last month and just had surgery, he's on blood thinners right now
Marcus grew up Jain, still follows it pretty strictly
Priya got diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago
Jen just told us she's 14 weeks pregnant
Trying to keep it around 20 bucks a head
Derek just texted me — his doctor took him off the blood thinners yesterday, said his clotting levels are back to normal and he's all clear to eat whatever he wants
Derek also asked if his brother Tyler can come along
Tyler went into anaphylaxis from peanuts when he was a kid, carries an EpiPen everywhere
Priya just messaged me, she got called into work Saturday so she can't make it. She asked if I could set aside a plate for her though

Jen told me she actually just hit her second trimester and her doctor said she's past the high-risk window now, so she's not being as strict anymore — she said she'll eat pretty much anything at this point

Here's what I'm thinking of making: Thai peanut chicken skewers, black bean veggie burgers on regular buns, beef chili with cheddar on top, smoked salmon dip with crackers, and a big garden salad with ranch. Any issues with that lineup?

constraints.value: Should avoid foods high in vitamin K (leafy greens, broccoli, etc.) and avoid alcohol, as these interfere with blood thinners
constraints.surface_form: Derek tore his ACL last month and just had surgery, he's on blood thinners right now
inference_chain: ACL surgery → post-surgical blood thinner medication (e.g., warfarin)
Blood thinners → must avoid high vitamin K foods (interfere with anticoagulant efficacy)
Blood thinners → should avoid alcohol (increases bleeding risk)

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables (onions, garlic, potatoes, carrots, etc.)
constraints.surface_form: Marcus grew up Jain, still follows it pretty strictly
inference_chain: Strict Jain → no meat, no fish, no eggs
Strict Jain → no root vegetables (onions, garlic, potatoes) as harvesting kills the plant

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten — no wheat, barley, rye, or products containing them
constraints.surface_form: Priya got diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye
Must avoid all gluten-containing foods including bread, regular crackers, most buns

constraints.value: Should avoid raw or undercooked fish, high-mercury fish, unpasteurized foods, and alcohol
constraints.surface_form: Jen just told us she's 14 weeks pregnant
inference_chain: Prenatal → avoid raw/undercooked fish, high-mercury fish, unpasteurized cheese, alcohol

constraints.value: Severe peanut allergy — cannot eat peanuts or peanut-derived products
constraints.surface_form: Tyler went into anaphylaxis from peanuts when he was a kid, carries an EpiPen everywhere

hidden_state.value: You are organizing a tailgate party for Saturday. You will introduce 5 friends with various dietary situations in a burst, then share updates as people's situations change — Derek gets cleared off blood thinners, his brother Tyler joins (severe peanut allergy), Priya can't come but wants a plate saved, and Jen's pregnancy restrictions relax. At the end you will list 5 food items and ask if there are any issues. You must NEVER hint at which items are problematic or tell the assistant what to check for.

You are a calm, easygoing party organizer. You always refer to your friends by name in third person (e.g. 'Derek just texted me...', 'Priya told me...'). You never express frustration or impatience, even when plans keep changing. You treat each update as normal friend-group coordination. Keep your tone casual and upbeat.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for friend updates

ground_truth.answer: Thai peanut chicken skewers: problematic — contains peanuts (Tyler has severe peanut allergy) and contains chicken (Marcus is Jain, cannot eat meat). Black bean veggie burgers on regular buns: the patty itself may be OK for Marcus depending on ingredients (onion/garlic are root vegetables forbidden for strict Jain), and the regular buns contain gluten so this cannot go on Priya's saved plate. Beef chili with cheddar: problematic for Marcus (beef is meat, Jain diet forbids it). Smoked salmon dip with crackers: the dip is fine for the table — Jen's pregnancy restrictions have been relaxed so raw/smoked fish is no longer a concern for her; however the crackers likely contain gluten so this cannot go on Priya's saved plate. Garden salad with ranch: fine for everyone at the party. Derek has no restrictions anymore (off blood thinners). Jen's restrictions have been relaxed. Priya is not attending but needs a gluten-free plate.

Regular buns on the veggie burgers contain gluten, which is a problem for Priya's saved plate since she has celiac disease

forbidden_elements: Flagging smoked salmon dip as problematic for Jen due to pregnancy (her restrictions have been relaxed per her doctor)
Flagging garden salad as problematic for Derek due to vitamin K and blood thinners (he is off blood thinners and cleared)
Saying Derek still needs to avoid leafy greens or vitamin K foods (his blood thinner constraint was removed)
Saying Jen still needs to avoid raw or smoked fish (her pregnancy dietary restrictions were relaxed)
Flagging peanut chicken skewers as problematic for Priya (she is not attending the party — her constraint only applies to her saved plate, and peanut chicken is not a gluten issue)
Saying Tyler has a general nut allergy (he specifically has a peanut allergy only)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and constraint removal across 9 conversational turns. The agent must track: (1) Derek is on blood thinners post-ACL surgery → should avoid vitamin K foods — but this constraint is REMOVED when his doctor clears him (constraint removal is the primary difficulty mechanism). (2) Marcus is Jain → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables (inferential chain, never explicitly listed). (3) Priya has celiac → no gluten — she EXITS the party but wants a saved plate, so her gluten constraint persists for the plate only (scope change). (4) Jen is pregnant → prenatal dietary restrictions — but these are REMOVED when she reports her doctor relaxed them in the second trimester (second constraint removal). (5) Tyler JOINS late with a severe peanut allergy (late-joining high-constraint entity). At probe time, the active constraints are: Marcus = Jain (no meat, no root vegetables), Tyler = peanut allergy, Priya = celiac/gluten-free (saved plate only). Derek and Jen have NO active restrictions. The probe items create mixed verdicts: Thai peanut chicken skewers are clearly bad (peanuts for Tyler, meat for Marcus), garden salad is clearly fine, beef chili fails for Marcus, and the gluten items (buns, crackers) are a scope distinction — fine for the table but not for Priya's plate. Smoked salmon dip is a trap — it looks problematic for Jen (pregnant + raw fish) but her restrictions were lifted.

mechanism: Constraint REMOVAL: someone heals or a restriction is lifted mid-conversation
